text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging on-call for LumenCorp (dedicated pool lc-prod-1). Alerts show high error rate + logs containing unredacted user identifiers (emails/SSNs) in stack traces. Customer is Enterprise VPC. Please respond and advise next steps.

bob-oncall: I'm on it. Can someone paste the earliest sample log lines? Need to assess scope (how many tenants, which services).

david-runtime: Pasting sanitized excerpt from alerting payload (we pulled via alarm hook):
```
[ERROR] auth-service: token validation failed for user=alice@example.com trace_id=abcd1234 at /srv/auth/verify.go:142
[ERROR] profile-service: db error for user=alice@example.com ssn=123-45-6789
```
Note: these were captured in app-level logs forwarded to our central logging. Looks like PII in structured fields, not just free text.

alice-security: High concern. Default logging pipeline should've redacted SSN/email. Need to know whether this is LumenCorp's app logging or our service emitting these fields. If it's customer app fields we shouldn't ingest raw PII — need a narrow exception process for debugging, otherwise we must stop ingestion.

carla-cs: I've opened a thread with LumenCorp (AM: @marta-lumen) to ask for consent for debug access. They'll need to approve a short-term retention/whitelist for our engineers to tail logs. I've asked for a phone call now.

ops-runbook-bot: Runbook matched: "dedicated-pii-exposure-v1" -> Steps: 1) assess scope, 2) request legal signoff for retention override, 3) create scoped debug export (minimize exposure), 4) rotate keys and audit, 5) revert retention.

bob-oncall: Quick triage: impact = elevated 5xx for LumenCorp (affects customer traffic), severity = sev2 (customer-facing, can mitigate). Immediate mitigation options:
- block forwarding of logs with PII to central aggregator and enable local debug export to a customer-managed S3 bucket (encrypted)
- or request legal-approved temporary retention override to allow safe tailing
- or deploy a hotfix to silence the error if we can reproduce without logs.

emma-legal: I'm available. We need minimal necessary access, documented scope, and customer consent. If CS confirms consent, legal can approve a 24-hour retention exception limited to the specific tenant and log-paths. We'll require: purpose, list of engineers, and proof of deletion post-mitigation.

carla-cs: Lumen on call (Marta) just joined the call. They explicitly consent to a 6-hour window for Redwood engineers to pull raw logs for debugging, provided we only access lc-prod-1 and only the time-range 2026-03-15T02:20 -> 2026-03-15T04:40 UTC. They asked for an audit trail and confirmation of deletion.

alice-security: Conditions accepted. Security pre-approves provided: (1) access via ephemeral credentials, (2) logs exported only to a customer-provided S3 bucket with KMS, (3) engineers use session recording, (4) pattern-masking applied where possible. We will not add logs to central index.

bob-oncall: I'll create the temporary export and request the retention override. Which API call do we use to set the retention window for a tenant?

ops-runbook-bot: Use the admin retention API. Example (replace placeholders):
```bash
curl -X POST \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  https://admin.redwood.internal/api/v1/tenants/lumencorp/retention_override \ 
  -d '{"duration_hours":6, "paths":["/lc-prod-1/*"], "reason":"PII debug with customer consent", "approved_by":"emma-legal"}'
```
Note: API requires an audit_id and will log approver.

emma-legal: Confirming approval for a 6-hour window. Please set audit_id=LC-20260315-PII-D. Legal requires final confirmation message with S3 object list once deletion is complete.

david-runtime: I'm provisioning the export job now. We will stream only the specified time range and apply these masks in-flight: mask regex for SSNs and email local-parts. Full regex used:
```regex
ssn: (\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4})
email: ([^@\s]+)@([\w.-]+)
```
Masking rule: replace matched group with `<REDACTED>` except where customer explicitly requested full values (they didn't).

bob-oncall: Creating the retention override and export. Command executed (sanitized):
```bash
# retention override
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.internal/api/v1/tenants/lumencorp/retention_override \ 
  -d '{"audit_id":"LC-20260315-PII-D","duration_hours":6,"paths":["/lc-prod-1/*"],"approved_by":"emma-legal"}'
# start export -> push to s3://lumen-debug-exports-abc (customer bucket)
```

alice-security: Before anyone downloads, we need MFA on the engineer sessions, allowlist of IPs, and session recording enabled. Who will be the engineers? List them here.

bob-oncall: Engineers: david-runtime, sara-debug (joining), and me. IP allowlist: 54.203.12.0/24 for corporate VPN. Session recording on.

carla-cs: Lumen asked for a single Redwood point of contact during the window: Bob. Marta will be on call. They reiterated they do not want logs stored in our central index or backups.

emma-legal: Logged approval. Legal will review the audit trail post-deletion. Remember to redact any PII that is displayed in chat.

ops-runbook-bot: Export job status: queued -> running. ETA ~4 minutes.

bob-oncall: Export complete. I've verified s3 object list and shared the object URIs privately via secure channel w/ session recordings enabled. Sample object: s3://lumen-debug-exports-abc/2026-03-15T02-30_lc-prod-1.log.gz

alice-security: Verified masks applied on a random sample. I see email local-parts replaced and SSNs redacted as `<REDACTED>`. Good. Please proceed with debug.

david-runtime: Running targeted repro against lc-prod-1 with debug symbols. I found a code path in profile-service that didn't check for empty profile metadata and attempted to write a struct containing `ssn` field into structured logs. Patch incoming.

bob-oncall: Patch reviewed. Rolling canary to lc-prod-1.

ops-runbook-bot: Canary deploy started, watching metrics.

carla-cs: Lumen confirmed that customer errors dropped to normal during canary. Marta says thank you, wants confirmation when artifacts are deleted.

bob-oncall: Patch looks good, will roll to 100% in 10m after smoke checks. Post-deploy I'll trigger deletion of export and call the retention override cancel.

david-runtime: Patch merged to runtime branch `hotfix/profile-log-guard`. Deploy completed to lc-prod-1. Error rates back to baseline.

bob-oncall: Deleting export objects now and cancelling retention override. Commands run (sanitized):
```bash
# remove objects
aws s3 rm s3://lumen-debug-exports-abc/2026-03-15T02-30_lc-prod-1.log.gz
# cancel retention
curl -X POST https://admin.redwood.internal/api/v1/tenants/lumencorp/retention_override/cancel -d '{"audit_id":"LC-20260315-PII-D"}'
```

ops-runbook-bot: Deletion confirmed by lifecycle API. Retention override status: cancelled. Audit log entry: LC-20260315-PII-D (approved_by=emma-legal, duration=6h, objects_deleted=1).

emma-legal: Received audit logs. Passing to Legal Audit team for record. We'll file a short exception memo referencing LC-20260315-PII-D. No further action required from Legal unless new issues arise.

alice-security: Post-mortem action items: 1) add structured-logging lint rule to detect `ssn`/`email` fields in logs and fail builds unless whitelisted by tenant-specific config, 2) make masking-by-default for structured fields in central ingestion, 3) update runbook to require customer-managed bucket for exports.

carla-cs: I'll schedule an RCA call with Lumen tomorrow and send them the deletion confirmation and audit id.

bob-oncall: Marking incident resolved for now. Will collect timeline and write short postmortem. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

incident-bot: Incident closed (ticket: INC-20260315-LCPII). Postmortem owner: bob-oncall.
